To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ratiometric method can be used to quantify hormone ratios in thick samples of legume roots and nodules, (2) auxin/cytokinins ratios are distinct in different cell types of nodules and roots, and (3) the ratios are consistent with the role of auxin and cytokinins in the regulation of nodule development.
auxin and cytokinins have distinct spatio-temporal distributions in root and nodules of soybean, and that the auxin/cytokinins ratios correspond to distinct nodule cells types.
auxin and cytokinins act in a coordinated manner to control cell type identity in nodules of soybean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of quantitative 3D imaging methods for plant hormone signalling and their application to legume-rhizobium nodulation.
the development of new tools to study the spatio-temporal distribution of plant hormones in plant tissues, and the application of these tools for the investigation of hormone signalling in legumes.
developing new imaging methods for studying hormone responses in legume roots and nodules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratiometric imaging approach presented here is a valuable addition to the arsenal of tools that can be used to study the role of hormones during nodule development.
the auxin/cytokinins ratio is a key determinant for cell identity in the nodule.
the auxin/cytokinins ratios in the soybean nodule are a major determinant of cell identity and differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for accurate and quantitative 3-dimensional monitoring of hormone outputs in root tissues and applied this method to determine auxin and cytokinins outputs and ratios in soybean root and nodules.
the auxin/cytokinins ratio is a key determinant of cell fate and identity in soybean root and nodule development.

we have developed an imaging tool to monitor auxin and cytokinins outputs in a single experiment and that this tool can be used to study the spatio-temporal dynamics of auxin and cytokinnin signalling in legumes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of 3D ratiometric imaging of hormone outputs can be used to determine hormone response ratios in thick root and noder samples, a technique that can be extended to many other systems.
ratiometric imaging of auxin and cytokinins can be used to accurately determine hormone ratios at the cell level in 3D.
ratiometric imaging of auxin and cytokinins can be used for high throughput analysis of hormone ratios in thick plant tissues.
